text.p01: To everyone carrying something inside: you can set it down. A story about sharing our feelings and the friends who listen.
text.p03: Down by the willow brook lived a little turtle named Tavi. She had a smooth green shell and a big, quiet heart.
text.p04: Her best friend was Fern, a long-eared hare who said whatever she felt, the moment she felt it.
text.p05: One day the frogs laughed. "Slowpoke Tavi!" It stung. But Tavi only said, "I'm fine," and tucked the hurt inside, like a little pebble.
text.p06: When she wanted to tell Fern, "You're my best friend," her cheeks went hot. So she tucked that inside too. Click.
text.p07: A worry about the thunder. Click. A "no, thank you" she was afraid to say. Click. A wonderful idea for a game. Click.
text.p08: Keeping quiet felt safe. No one could laugh. No one could get it wrong. No one could say no.
text.p09: But pebble by pebble, Tavi's shell grew heavy. She walked slower and slower, and she couldn't climb Clover Hill anymore.
text.p10: "Come and play hop-stones!" called Fern. "Not today," said Tavi. Her shell was far too heavy to hop.
text.p11: At night, the pebbles rattled inside her. There was so little room left that Tavi couldn't find her own giggle.
text.p12: Everything she kept inside was safe. But Tavi felt heavy, and grey, and very far away from everyone.
text.p13: One evening, Fern sat down beside her. "You've been so quiet," she said softly. "Is something heavy?"
text.p14: "I'm fine," said Tavi. Click. Fern didn't push. She just stayed. "I'm here," she said, "whenever you're ready."
text.p15: The stars came out. Slowly, Tavi took out one tiny pebble. "When the frogs laughed at me… it hurt," she whispered.
text.p16: Fern didn't laugh. She leaned close. "Thank you for telling me. That would hurt me too." And the pebble felt lighter.
text.p17: So Tavi took out another. "I'm scared of thunder." And another. "I have a wonderful idea for a game!"
text.p18: Then the biggest one of all: "Fern… you're my best friend." "And you're mine!" cried Fern. Tavi felt as light as a leaf!
text.p19: Now there was a little pile of pebbles in the grass, every one a different color. "What should we do with them?" asked Tavi.
text.p20: Fern grinned. "Let's build something." One by one, they set the pebbles in the brook.
text.p21: The little frog hopped over with a pebble of his own. "I laughed because I was scared they'd laugh at me," he said. "I'm sorry."
text.p22: The duck brought one. The hedgehog brought one. Soon everyone was setting down the things they had kept inside.
text.p23: Pebble by pebble, a path of stepping stones grew across the brook, and everyone crossed it together.
text.p24: Feelings kept inside grow heavy. Feelings we share become a path. The End
text.cover: The Pebbles Inside. A Story About Sharing Our Feelings and the Friends Who Listen
